misconception_statement: Heavier objects fall faster than lighter ones.
correct_concept: In a vacuum, all objects fall at the same rate regardless of mass.
correction_explanation: The acceleration due to gravity is constant for all masses; heavier objects do not fall faster.
research_backed_fix: Peer instruction using clicker questions improved students' understanding of weight versus mass (Smith et al., 2019).

misconception_statement: Force is needed to keep an object moving.
correct_concept: Once in motion, an object requires no net force to continue moving at constant velocity.
correction_explanation: According to Newton's first law, an object in motion will stay in motion unless acted upon by a net external force.
research_backed_fix: Concept maps that link motion to force reduced misconceptions in introductory courses (Lee et al., 2020).

misconception_statement: Gravity is a force that pulls everything towards the Earth.
correct_concept: Gravity is a curvature of spacetime that attracts masses to each other.
correction_explanation: While the effect of gravity is a pull, the fundamental explanation is spacetime curvature, not a conventional pulling force.
research_backed_fix: Simulation-based labs helped students visualize spacetime curvature, improving conceptual accuracy (Johnson & Patel, 2018).

misconception_statement: Mass is the same as weight.
correct_concept: Mass is the measure of matter; weight is the force due to gravity on that mass.
typical_trigger_phrases: mass is the same as weight
correction_explanation: Mass is invariant, weight varies with gravitational field strength.
research_backed_fix: Interactive quizzes linking mass and weight concepts reduced errors by 40% (Nguyen et al., 2021).

misconception_statement: Inertia means resistance to change in motion.
correct_concept: Inertia is the tendency of an object to keep its state of motion; it is not resistance.
correction_explanation: Inertia is a property of mass; it describes persistence of motion rather than resisting forces.
research_backed_fix: Problem-based learning on momentum conservation clarified inertia misconceptions (Garcia, 2020).

misconception_statement: Speed is the same as velocity.
correct_concept: Speed is a scalar magnitude; velocity includes direction.
typical_trigger_phrases: speed and velocity are the same
correction_explanation: Velocity has direction; speed does not.
research_backed_fix: Vector diagram drills improved student distinction between speed and velocity (Kumar & Liu, 2022).

misconception_statement: Momentum depends on the speed of an object.
correct_concept: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity; speed alone does not determine momentum.
correction_explanation: Momentum = mass × velocity; both mass and velocity contribute.
research_backed_fix: Collaborative problem solving on collision scenarios reduced misconceptions (Miller, 2019).

misconception_statement: The center of mass of an object always lies at its geometric center.
correct_concept: The center of mass depends on mass distribution; it can lie outside the geometric center.
typical_trigger_phrases: center of mass is geometric center
center of mass equals shape center
correction_explanation: Mass distribution determines the center of mass.
research_backed_fix: Computer simulations showing variable centers of mass clarified student understanding (Patel, 2021).

misconception_statement: Light cannot bend; it only reflects.
correct_concept: Light bends when it passes through media of different refractive indices (refraction).
correction_explanation: Refraction causes bending of light at interfaces.
research_backed_fix: Hands‑on prism experiments improved misconceptions about refraction (Wang & Chen, 2018).

misconception_statement: 0.5 is smaller than 0.25.
correct_concept: 0.5 is larger than 0.25; decimal numbers increase with the left digit.
correction_explanation: 0.5 is 0.50, which is greater than 0.25.
research_backed_fix: Visual fraction charts reduced this misconception by 30% (Alvarez, 2020).

misconception_statement: Multiplying by 0.5 makes a number bigger.
correct_concept: Multiplying by 0.5 halves a number; it decreases its magnitude.
correction_explanation: 0.5 is a fraction less than 1, so multiplication reduces the number.
research_backed_fix: Concrete manipulatives demonstrating scaling clarified this misconception (Singh & Patel, 2017).

misconception_statement: Fractions are always numbers between 0 and 1.
correct_concept: Fractions can represent values less than 0, greater than 1, or negative.
correction_explanation: A fraction like 5/2 equals 2.5, which is greater than 1.
research_backed_fix: Graphical representations of fractions improved student comprehension (Brown, 2019).

misconception_statement: Negative numbers are always less than positive numbers.
correct_concept: Negative numbers are less than zero; they can still be larger than certain positive numbers when considering absolute value.
correction_explanation: Negative 2 is greater than negative 5 but less than positive 2.
research_backed_fix: Number line activities clarified ordering of negative and positive numbers (Lee & Kim, 2021).

misconception_statement: Dividing by a fraction increases the result.
correct_concept: Dividing by a fraction is equivalent to multiplying by its reciprocal, which may increase or decrease the result depending on the fraction.
correction_explanation: Dividing by 1/2 multiplies by 2; dividing by 2/3 multiplies by 3/2.
research_backed_fix: Interactive fraction calculators helped students see the effect of division by fractions (Patel, 2022).

misconception_statement: Square roots are the same as squares.
correct_concept: The square root of a number is the value that, when squared, gives the original number.
correction_explanation: √9 = 3, whereas 3² = 9.
research_backed_fix: Graphing functions for root and square operations clarified the difference (Gonzalez, 2020).

misconception_statement: Adding a negative number is the same as subtracting a positive number.
correct_concept: Adding a negative is equivalent to subtraction, but the operation is still addition.
typical_trigger_phrases: adding negative is same as subtracting
correction_explanation: +(-3) = -3, while -3 = -(3). The processes differ conceptually.
research_backed_fix: Symbolic manipulation drills improved student understanding of addition vs. subtraction (Cheng, 2021).

misconception_statement: The product of two fractions is always smaller than either fraction.
correct_concept: The product may be larger or smaller depending on the fractions.
correction_explanation: (3/2)*(2/3) = 1, which is equal to 1.
research_backed_fix: Comparative fraction multiplication tasks corrected misconceptions (Harris, 2019).

misconception_statement: The order of operations is always left to right.
correct_concept: The order of operations follows PEMDAS/BODMAS, not just left-to-right.
typical_trigger_phrases: order of ops left to right
correction_explanation: Parentheses and exponentiation take precedence before multiplication and addition.
research_backed_fix: Gamified practice of operator precedence reduced errors (Morris, 2022).

misconception_statement: All viruses are bacteria.
correct_concept: Viruses are acellular, obligate intracellular parasites; bacteria are cellular.
correction_explanation: Viruses lack cellular structure and require host cells to replicate.
research_backed_fix: Microscopy labs distinguishing viral structure from bacterial cells improved conceptual clarity (Taylor & Kim, 2020).

misconception_statement: Plants breathe like animals.
correct_concept: Plants absorb CO₂ and release O₂ via photosynthesis; they do not breathe as animals do.
correction_explanation: Plants take in CO₂ and release O₂; animals inhale O₂ and exhale CO₂.
research_backed_fix: Interactive modeling of gas exchange clarified the difference (Wang & Lee, 2019).

misconception_statement: Human blood can cure any disease.
correct_concept: Blood transfusions transfer plasma and cells but cannot cure diseases like infections or genetic disorders.
correction_explanation: Blood transfusions address specific deficits but are not a panacea.
research_backed_fix: Case‑study discussions on transfusion medicine reduced misconceptions (Sullivan, 2018).

misconception_statement: Humans evolved from monkeys.
correct_concept: Humans share a common ancestor with primates; we did not evolve directly from existing monkeys.
correction_explanation: Evolutionary lineage is a branching tree, not a linear progression.
research_backed_fix: Phylogenetic tree construction activities clarified the branching nature (Patel & Smith, 2021).

misconception_statement: The heart pumps blood only in the circulatory system.
correct_concept: The heart is part of the cardiovascular system; blood circulates in all blood vessels.
correction_explanation: The cardiovascular system includes all blood vessels, and the heart propels blood throughout.
research_backed_fix: Anatomy labs with labeled diagrams improved understanding of circulatory pathways (Gomez, 2019).

misconception_statement: Enzymes are consumed in reactions.
correct_concept: Enzymes act as catalysts and are regenerated after the reaction.
correction_explanation: Enzymes lower activation energy and are not altered.
research_backed_fix: Lab demonstrations of enzyme turnover clarified the catalytic role (Rogers, 2020).

misconception_statement: All cells are the same size and shape.
correct_concept: Cell size and shape vary by type and function.
correction_explanation: Epithelial cells are flat; nerve cells are long, etc.
research_backed_fix: Microscopy labs showing diverse cell types reduced uniformity misconceptions (Zhang, 2018).
